overview: Use cursor pagination, ID normalization and a variable-height virtualized list. Anchor by post ID plus pixel offset rather than raw scrollTop. Keep new posts behind a New posts button to avoid moving the reader. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.result: DOM work scales with the window; retained data still needs an independent bound
estimation.implication: Profile scrolling, image decode and memory; preserve focused rows when windowing.

components.rationale: Own this responsibility at the Browser / User boundary; keep communication explicit through the diagrammed dependency.

components.purpose: Use cursor pagination, ID normalization and a variable-height virtualized list. Anchor by post ID plus pixel offset rather than raw scrollTop. Keep new posts behind a New posts button to avoid moving the reader. Performance plan: 10,000 browsed posts, 20 fetched per page; illustrative mounted window of 20 plus 10 overscan; lazy images with reserved aspect ratio. Accessibility: Use semantic articles and headings, keyboard-operable like/load-more controls, polite load announcements and stable focus when rows are recycled. Never announce the whole feed on every update. Failure recovery: Track mutationId and server version; rollback only the failed optimistic operation. Dedup page IDs, expose retry and retain existing content. Trade-off: A simple paginated list has better navigation semantics for shorter feeds; virtualization helps very long sessions but complicates variable heights and accessibility.

flows.title: Local interaction, state transition and UI update

steps.title: Receive user intent
steps.explanation: Fetch cursor pages and deduplicate posts. Use semantic articles and headings, keyboard-operable like/load-more controls, polite load announcements and stable focus when rows are recycled. Never announce the whole feed on every update.

steps.title: Apply the owning transition
steps.explanation: Use cursor pagination, ID normalization and a variable-height virtualized list. Anchor by post ID plus pixel offset rather than raw scrollTop. Keep new posts behind a New posts button to avoid moving the reader.

steps.title: Render controlled child state
steps.explanation: 10,000 browsed posts, 20 fetched per page; illustrative mounted window of 20 plus 10 overscan; lazy images with reserved aspect ratio. Child events return to the owner; focus and selection use stable identities.

steps.title: Capture user intent without duplicating authority
steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call PUT /posts/{id}/like through the API adapter. Request: {liked:true, mutationId:"m1", expectedVersion:3}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: Track mutationId and server version; rollback only the failed optimistic operation. Dedup page IDs, expose retry and retain existing content. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

failureCases.scenario: A like retry and a new page return conflicting versions
failureCases.handling: Track mutationId and server version; rollback only the failed optimistic operation. Dedup page IDs, expose retry and retain existing content.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.

alternatives: A simple paginated list has better navigation semantics for shorter feeds; virtualization helps very long sessions but complicates variable heights and accessibility.
